[THOUGHT] The dermatologic exam reveals three small (2–3 mm), dome-shaped, hardened papules with central umbilication — a classic morphologic hallmark of molluscum contagiosum. This viral infection (caused by MCV) commonly presents as discrete, flesh-colored or pearly, umbilicated papules, often on exposed or intertriginous skin. The absence of pruritus aligns with typical presentation. Other umbilicated lesions (e.g., verrucae) usually lack the characteristic central dimple and are more hyperkeratotic; basal cell carcinoma is exceedingly unlikely in this context given age-agnostic presentation, size, and lack of ulceration or telangiectasia. No systemic symptoms or immunosuppression were mentioned, supporting typical self-limited molluscum. At this point, clinical diagnosis is highly reliable — no further testing is needed to confirm.

[DIAGNOSIS] Molluscum contagiosum
